title: Top-degree torsion integration for flat compactifiable morphisms
statement:
Let $h:V\to S$ be a flat, separated morphism of finite presentation between Noetherian schemes (each admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), with flatness and finite presentation as in [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], compactifiable in the sense that $h=rj$ with $j$ an open immersion and $r$ proper [def-asd-compactifiable, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Suppose that all its nonempty geometric fibres have pure dimension $d\geq0$. Let $N\geq1$ be invertible on $S$, put $R=\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$, and work on the ordinary small etale sites and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For any sheaf $F$ of $R$-modules on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ put $F(d)=F\otimes_R\mu_N^{\otimes_R d}$, where $\mu_N$ is the etale sheaf $U\mapsto\{z\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:z^N=1\}$, and the zeroth tensor power is $R$ [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback, def-kun-derived-tensor].

There is a natural top-degree trace
$$\operatorname{tr}_{h,F}:R^{2d}h_!\bigl(h^*F(d)\bigr)\longrightarrow F.$$
Here $R^ih_!G=\mathcal H^i(Rh_!G)$, and $R^ih_!G=0$ for $i>2d$ for every sheaf $G$ of $R$-modules on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$. The trace is natural in $F$, commutes with change of Noetherian base under compact-support base change, and is transitive for compositions of such morphisms: if $g:W\to V$ is another such morphism of pure relative dimension $e$, then, under the canonical top-degree composition isomorphism $R^{2(d+e)}(hg)_!\cong R^{2d}h_!R^{2e}g_!$, the trace for $hg$ equals $\operatorname{tr}_{h,F}\circ R^{2d}h_!(\operatorname{tr}_{g,h^*F(d)})$, with the canonical pullback and twist identifications. These assertions include restriction to open subsets of $V$ (via extension by zero), and localization along separated etale source morphisms of finite type (via etale sum extension). In relative dimension zero for an etale morphism, it is the sum-of-sheets counit $h_!h^*F\to F$. For $\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ it is integration obtained by extension by zero into $\mathbf P^1_S$, whose trace sends the Kummer Chern class of $\mathcal O(1)$ to $1$; for $\mathbf A^d_S$ it is the ordered composite of these integrations (rank zero is the identity), hence the unit trace of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace].

The vanishing above defines a canonical map
$$t_{h,N}:Rh_!R_V(d)[2d]\longrightarrow R_S$$
by projection to $\mathcal H^{2d}$ followed by $\operatorname{tr}_{h,R}$. More generally, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, and let $K\in D^b(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. There is an $A$-linear derived trace
$$T^A_{h,K}:Rh_!\bigl(h^*K(d)[2d]\bigr)\longrightarrow K,$$
where $A(d)=\mu_N^{\otimes_R d}\otimes_R A$ and $K(d)=K\otimes_A^L A(d)$. This map is the composite of the inverse canonical projection-formula isomorphism
$$Rh_!\bigl(h^*K(d)[2d]\bigr)\ \cong\ K\otimes_R^L Rh_!R_V(d)[2d]$$
and $1_K\otimes_R^L t_{h,N}$, in the derived category of $A$-modules, with $K\otimes_R^L R\cong K$. This description agrees with the sheaf trace in top degree and has the same composition and etale normalization. If $N\mid N'$ with $N'$ invertible on $S$ and $N A=0$, the traces constructed using $N$ and $N'$ are identical under the twist identifications induced by $\mu_{N'}\to\mu_N$, $z\mapsto z^{N'/N}$. In particular the formula using any one common annihilator defines these maps for all such coefficient rings $A$. No assertion about the trace's adjoint being invertible is made.

source.place: XVIII 2.8 (pp. 552–553), Theorem 2.9 and Variances 1–4 (pp. 553–558), 2.10 (p. 559), 2.13.1–2.13.2 (p. 560); twisting independence 1.1.1 (pp. 484–485), composition at the derived level 3.2.4 (pp. 584–585). This is the top-degree torsion trace construction, before smooth duality 3.2.5; no Stacks tag for this normalized trace theorem was found.
